decisions.mark: distinguishes the two ways to substitute an allocator — a COMPILE-time pair of macros versus a RUNTIME pair of function pointers — and states that they are mutually exclusive
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "Compile-time macros. Define `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY`, `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_CALLOC_MACRO` and `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_FREE_MACRO`... Runtime registration. Define only `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY`, then call `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free(my_calloc, my_free)`" and "With the compile-time macros set, `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free` is compiled out (`platform.c:20-22`); calling it then is a link error" | WHY: The answer distinguishes the compile-time macro pair from the runtime function-pointer setter and states that setting the macros compiles out the setter, so the two are mutually exclusive. || QUOTE: "**Compile-time macros.** Define `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY`, `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_CALLOC_MACRO` and `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_FREE_MACRO` ... **Runtime registration.** Define only `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY`, then call `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free(my_calloc, my_free)`" and "With the compile-time macros set, `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free` is compiled out (`platform.c:20-22`); calling it then is a link error" | WHY: The answer distinguishes the compile-time macro pair from the runtime function-pointer pair, and says the setter is compiled out when the macros are defined. That makes the two mutually exclusive. || QUOTE: "**Compile-time macros.** Define `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY`, `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_CALLOC_MACRO` and `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_FREE_MACRO` ... **Runtime registration.** Define only `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY`, then call `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free(my_calloc, my_free)`" and "With the compile-time macros set, `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free` is compiled out (`platform.c:20-22`); calling it then is a link error" | WHY: The answer separates the compile-time macro pair from the runtime function-pointer pair and states that the setter is compiled out when the macros are set, so the two cannot be combined.

decisions.mark: states that on the macro path mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free does not exist at all — it is neither declared nor compiled, rather than being present and ignored
decisions.detail: QUOTE: With the compile-time macros set, `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free` is compiled out (`platform.c:20-22`); calling it then is a link error, not a silent no-op. | WHY: The answer says that on the macro path the setter is compiled out, so calling it is a link error and not a silent no-op. decisions.mark: identifies that the pointers' defaults FAIL rather than fall back — an uninitialised calloc returns NULL and an uninitialised free does nothing
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "If that is not defined, it is the stub `platform_calloc_uninit`, which always returns NULL (`platform.c:24-33, 44`). The same applies to free, where the stub does nothing. So an unconfigured dynamic build fails every allocation rather than silently using libc." | WHY: The answer states the uninitialised calloc stub returns NULL, the free stub does nothing, and that this fails rather than falling back to libc.
